newsitem.title: USA: Ashland had Q2 profit on refining loss.
newsitem.headline: Ashland had Q2 profit on refining loss.

text.p: Ashland Inc Thursday reported a small profit for its second quarter ending March 31, due to flooding which left it with a refining and marketing loss despite lower refining costs.

The company said it had second quarter net income of $7 million, or $0.03 a share. This compares to a loss of $2 million, or $0.11 per share, in the March quarter last year. Sales and operating revenues were $3.2 billion for the quarter just ended and $3.1 billion a year ago.
"Our results for the quarter were better than last year and in line with most analysts' expectations," said chief executive Paul W. Chellgren.
He noted the March quarter historically is the company's most difficult because of the seasonality of such businesses as gasoline marketing and road construction.
Chellgren said operating results were mixed with record results from Valvoline and Ashland Coal.
Operating income from Ashland Chemical, the company's leading profit contributor, was down somewhat but remained strong.
Equity income from Arch Mineral improved, while APAC operated slightly above break-even levels despite a winter slowdown in construction activity.

"These were all positive outcomes," Chellgren said. "On the other hand, our refining and marketing segment reported an operating loss, and operating income declined from our oil and gas exploration and production division."
Chellgren said SuperAmerica had a modest operating profit for the quarter while Ashland Petroleum had an operating loss.

"Heavy floods in the Ohio Valley hurt petroleum refining and marketing operations, limiting our ability to ship product on the river at a time when margins were strengthening," he noted. "These factors, higher average input costs and expenses related to previously announced staff reductions contributed to Ashland Petroleum's operating loss.

"We were pleased, however, by the significant decline in refining expenses, which declined $0.49 a barrel in the March quarter, continuing the trend of recent years. For the six months, refining expenses were down $0.31 a barrel.
SuperAmerica achieved higher gasoline and merchandise sales volumes and margins during the quarter.
